questions: Should the output consist of N numbers (one per i) separated by spaces, line breaks, or another format?
If multiple subsets of size K containing A_i achieve the same maximum GCD, does it matter which subset is chosen, or only the GCD value is required?
When K = 1, is the answer for each i simply A_i, or is there any special handling?
Are the elements considered distinct by position even if they have equal values, i.e., can the same value be chosen multiple times from different indices?
Must the chosen K elements be in their original order, or can they be any K elements regardless of order?
Is the GCD computed over the selected K values only, or does it involve any other elements (e.g., prefix/suffix)?
Are there any constraints on the size of the output numbers (e.g., should they be printed modulo some value)?
If N or K are at their maximum limits, are there any time or memory limits that affect the required algorithmic complexity?
answers: Each of the N answers should be printed on a separate line, i.e. the j-th line corresponds to the answer for i=j.
Only the maximum GCD value is required, not which subset achieves it.
Yes, when K=1 the only choice is A_i itself, so the answer is A_i.
Positions are treated as distinct even if values repeat, so equal values at different indices count as separate elements.
The order of the chosen K elements does not matter since GCD is order-independent.
Not specified beyond what's given; the GCD is computed only over the selected K values.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume standard integer output, no modulo is implied.
Not specified beyond what's given; assume standard algorithmic time/memory limits for this constraint size.
inline_prompts: You are given a sequence A = (A_1, A_2, \dots, A_N) of length N and a positive integer K (at most N). For each i = 1, 2, \dots, N, solve the following problem: When you choose K elements from A that include A_i, find the maximum possible GCD (greatest common divisor) of those chosen elements. Each of the N answers should be printed on a separate line, i.e. the j-th line corresponds to the answer for i=j. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N K A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print the result. Constraints - 1 \leq K \leq N \leq 1.2 \times 10^6 - 1 \leq A_i \leq 10^6 - All input values are integers.
